reason: The cited evidence does not address Mg-containing HEAs, their oxide layers, or Mg-rich intermetallic formation. E1 discusses Mg alloys processed by ball milling, E2 describes oxidation in an FeNiCuAlCr HEA without Mg, and E3 covers Al-Zr intermetallic coarsening in refractory superalloys. None of the key premises are supported by the provided passages.
premises: Mg-containing HEAs can be prepared in a uniform, metastable solid-solution state with a protective oxide layer.
At 800–1200 °C, diffusion drives nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
These precipitates disrupt the uniform distribution of oxide-forming species and the coherent oxide layer.
This disruption degrades corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
